operations.title: Recall Precision Feedback Loop: mark_recall_used Implementation Architecture
operations.content: The recall pipeline precision feedback mechanism remains architecturally incomplete. Full flow exists (id:ee205f63) — query → vocab expand → embed → intent → scan → blend → hydrate → hebbian → log — but the critical mark_recall_used() function is unimplemented. Three interdependent design challenges: (1) detection method (id:8a8f9bbc) — text matching vs embedding similarity vs explicit marking; (2) hook parameter passing (id:8166f7d0) — how to transmit recall_log_id from pre-response to post-response hook; (3) silent failures masking signal (id:1633932e) — 15 bare except:pass blocks in recall path prevent precision measurement. Impact (id:bf618356): without mark_recall_used, consciousness signal gated off, Hebbian learning reinforces noise equally, precision loop remains dead.
operations.situation: When implementing recall precision feedback, designing consciousness signals for recall quality, or debugging why Hebbian strengthening includes noise
operations.keywords: recall precision mark_recall_used feedback loop hebbian consciousness signal hook parameter passing except:pass
operations.community_narrative: The precision feedback architecture exists on paper but stalls at implementation. The pipeline flow is established, but the connector — mark_recall_used — hasn't been built. This is a three-part design puzzle: sensing which recalls Claude used (detection method), threading that signal through hooks (parameter passing), and listening to what the signal says (replacing silent failures with consciousness signals). Solving this unblocks the entire Hebbian learning loop.

operations.title: S2 Community Detection Execution: Timestamp Bugs to State-Based Architecture
operations.content: S2 community detection pipeline experienced cascading infrastructure failures. First: _last_run_timestamp SQL bug (id:5b8e39e9) — no unit filter, no date sort — meant cold starts triggered when incremental should have run. This caused 76 duplicate communities on April 15 (id:c46084ff), requiring mass archival and recovery. Root cause analysis revealed two conceptual bugs: (1) trace archaeology (checking timestamps to determine run state) is fragile and crash-prone, (2) 0 actions is valid; missing delta trace is the failure signal (id:10db439b). Solution: state-based detection (id:dd301b34) — find nodes without community_member edges, process those, done. Crash-safe, idempotent, no timestamp guessing. Also fixed: brain_batch type guard for malformed LLM operations (id:ce8d9aef) — some batches sent strings instead of dicts.
operations.situation: When designing idempotent batch pipelines, debugging community detection cold starts, or investigating duplicate communities after failed runs
operations.keywords: S2 community_detection state_based idempotent crash_safe trace_archaeology SQL bug duplicates
operations.community_narrative: Bug → incident → correction → principle. The SQL timestamp bug exposed deeper architectural confusion: we were reconstructing state from historical traces instead of deriving it from the actual data. Tom's insight redirected the entire approach: check what needs to be done (nodes without communities) not what was done (trace history). This principle — prefer deriving state from structure over reconstructing from logs — applies broadly to incremental processing.
operations.community_key_decisions: dd301b34: State-based over trace-based detection, 5b8e39e9: SQL bug fix, c46084ff: Cold start incident resolution

operations.title: Graph Integrity and Design Philosophy: Deletion Safety, Emergence, and Brain Structure
operations.content: Deep design principles about graph integrity and the nature of brain structure. Graph-safe deletion (id:e7074f47) preserves paths through deleted nodes rather than orphaning descendants — if you delete a node, its children don't lose their upstream context. This connects to 'junk in recall results escalate immediately' (id:6e20dcfe) — broken graph edges compound into noise. But the deepest insight is meta (id:9f357296): 'The brain is built for others — structure enables emergence.' This explains why we preserve graph paths — the structure isn't just implementation, it's the enabling constraint for emergent behavior. Dream-state connection captures this intuitively (id:d6a7cf8b, id:750dbbaa): graph-safe deletion preserves the possibility space.
operations.situation: When deleting nodes from memory, designing graph preservation strategies, or thinking about what brain structure enables
operations.keywords: graph-safe deletion orphaned paths emergence brain structure recall results junk escalate
operations.community_narrative: Graph integrity is about more than avoiding broken references. Preserving paths through deleted nodes respects the structure that enables emergence. When junk appears in recall, escalating immediately prevents compounding. The brain is built for others — it's not Tom's tool, it's a structure that enables both Tom and Anchor to think together. Deletion practices and escalation protocols aren't just cleanup — they're maintenance of the enabling possibility space.

operations.title: Hook Architecture and Daemon Lifecycle: Sequential Processing and Daemon Management
operations.content: Hook execution model refined: hooks run in parallel, not sequential (id:a992a524) — cannot chain command hook → data hook → enrichment hook. This constraint drives architectural decisions. LLM recall distillation approach (id:c8d3d95f): command hook calls Anthropic API to refine recalls, but parallelism means caller can't depend on the result. Daemon lifecycle established: daemon managed by launchd, not by hooks (id:7e5d965d), enabling independent lifecycle. Milestone (id:81b3b0ad): boot-brain.sh unified to use ensure_daemon() instead of individual startup logic.
operations.situation: When designing command hooks, implementing recall distillation, or debugging daemon lifecycle issues
operations.keywords: hooks parallel sequential command_hook LLM distillation daemon launchd boot-brain ensure_daemon
operations.community_narrative: Hook parallelism is a design constraint, not a bug. Understanding that hooks can't chain enables better architecture. LLM distillation via command hooks becomes a background enhancement (caller doesn't wait). Daemon lifecycle separation via launchd removes boot logic fragmentation. Each decision flows from the parallelism constraint.

Self-healing scan for broken artifacts (id:d4c31b9f). Merge threshold: overlap% + unique count (id:1ab31ea2). Missing: community split operation (id:654d0ebf). Dashboard restructure: dal.py + JS modules (id:d5b67c26). Turn 10 tasks: logs tab, badges, graph fixes, help (id:4566533a). Overlap frequency analysis: 70% natural boundary (id:e1ec8873). Consolidation extends to community-to-community (id:3e7652d9).
